summary.one_liner: ipdb is a drop-in replacement for Python's pdb debugger that uses the IPython debugger, adding tab completion, syntax highlighting and better tracebacks.
summary.what_it_does: Exports functions (set_trace, pm, run, runcall, runeval) that mirror the standard pdb module but drop into the IPython debugger. The set_trace function takes a context argument for how many lines of source to show and a cond argument to break only when a condition is true. Context size can also be set via the IPDB_CONTEXT_SIZE env var or a .ipdb, setup.cfg, or pyproject.toml file, with the env var taking priority. It provides a bin/ipdb script (and ipdb3) to run a script under the debugger, and a context manager (launch_ipdb_on_exception) and decorator (iex) that open the debugger when an exception is raised. The README also shows how to use it with pytest via --pdbcls.
use_cases: drop into a debugger at a breakpoint
inspect code with tab completion while debugging
notable: Drop-in replacement for pdb with the same interface, backed by the IPython debugger
Configurable context lines via env var, home config file, setup.cfg, or pyproject.toml
Command-line runner (ipdb script) for debugging whole scripts
Exception-triggered debugging via a with-statement context manager or @iex decorator
caveats: README documents Python 2 compatibility notes and version pins (ipdb==0.6, ipdb<=0.8) for old Python versions, so it is aimed at a mix of Python versions
Output of nose and other stdout-altering tools needs explicit sset_trace/spm variants, which the README calls brittle in earlier releases
